transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Jordan Lee (Redwood); Evan Morris, Priya Nair, Luis Ortega, Anna Kim (Skylark)

Auto-summary (may be fuzzy): quick status on creds, bench numbers, next steps for eu-west run and security docs exchange.

[00:00] Maya: All right folks, thanks for hopping on. This is our weekly sprint 4 POC check-in for Skylark. Quick roll call — Maya from Redwood here, Jordan also from my side. Over to you Evan?
[00:08] Evan: Hey everyone, Evan here.
[00:10] Priya: Priya, hi.
[00:12] Luis: Luis — product.
[00:13] Anna: Anna, DevOps.
[00:16] Maya: Great. I put the agenda in the chat: access gating, bench results we ran last week, and tuning / next steps. Jordan, do you want to kick to the bench recap?
[00:25] Jordan: Yeah, sure. So quick context — we ran a mixed traffic benchmark against the hosted endpoint and a dedicated small pool with 2x A100-equivalent GPUs. The script used your top-20 prompts that Anna uploaded, approx 1.2k mean tokens per request due to long receipts and chat history. Results: hosted median p50 latency 210ms per token, dedicated p50 165ms per token. Throughput on dedicated with batching was ~220 tokens/sec under steady-state with 4 concurrent streams.
[01:02] Priya: Sorry can I pause — when you say per-token, is that including the network hop back to our VPC?
[01:07] Jordan: Good call. These numbers are measured from our client in us-west-2 to the Redwood endpoint in eu-west originally, so they include internet path. For the dedicated run we ran within the same region to reduce cross-region. We also have a run that isolates pure inference time (no client network) — p50 token time was ~120ms on dedicated.
[01:28] Luis: Hmm, so for our SLOs we need tail latency <500ms for full responses under typical 300-token replies. Sounds promising but we need to see tail numbers. Any p95 or p99?
[01:40] Jordan: P95 was 640ms on hosted in that long-chain test; on dedicated p95 dropped to ~420ms. P99 still spikes occasionally — we saw a couple spikes around 1.6s tied to cold KV cache population.
[01:54] Anna: Can you explain KV cache — I think our infra team misheard it as K V cash yesterday — what is causing the cold spikes?
[02:02] Jordan: Sure. KV cache refers to key-value cache of the transformer past-key-values. When a new session hits a model variant that doesn't have warm KV entries, the runtime needs to populate the cache which can add latency for earlier tokens. We mitigate via sticky routing and a small warm-up burst. In your case, traffic pattern had a lot of unique session IDs so warm-up wasn't complete.
[02:25] Evan: Is there something we should change client-side? We could batch more or keep sessions sticky.
[02:30] Jordan: Yes, batching helps overall throughput but increases per-request latency for single user flows. For Skylark we're recommending a hybrid: small continuous batching (max batch 8) + session affinity for repeat shoppers to keep KV warm. We'll add a config snippet.
[02:47] Priya: On the security front, we still need details about KMS integration — we use Vault with an HSM-backed key in prod. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[02:58] Maya: Short answer: yes. Redwood Private supports KMS integration and bring-your-own-key in both Private deployments and Dedicated via our KMS bridge. For hosted we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with AWS KMS or a partner HSM, pending an ent contract.
[03:14] Priya: Ent contract — right. How about audit logs and retention? We need 7 years for certain flows — is that supported?
[03:21] Maya: We can retain audit logs in your account in Private, or for Dedicated we provide export to your SIEM with configurable retention. For hosted we can support long-term retention as an add-on; we'll send the compliance pack.
[03:33] Luis: One question on SSO — we tried the metadata you gave and got an error during our test. Anna, do you have the screenshot?
[03:41] Anna: Yeah I pasted the error in chat — assertion consumer service mismatch. Looks like the redirect URL wasn't correct.
[03:46] Maya: That usually means the ACS URL in the IdP doesn't match the SP config. Jordan, do we have the exact SP metadata?
[03:51] Jordan: I'll re-share the SP metadata — there was a small path change in our staging that slipped. I'll update the metadata and Priya can re-upload.
[03:58] Priya: Cool. We'll retry.
[04:00] Jordan: Back to benches — we also tried int8 quant profile on a smaller model variant; it lowered cost per token by ~30% but quality had a small regression on the refund policy prompts. We can run evals on your 50 prompt QA set to measure delta.
[04:17] Evan: We can't accept any meaningfully degraded quality on refund related flows. Can you quantify "small regression"?
[04:22] Jordan: Sure. On BLEU-like match of expected structured fields we saw a drop from 0.92 to 0.87 on that subset; in human review that's borderline. Our suggestion: keep larger model for refund path, use quantized smaller model for search/summary paths. This is where routing policies come in — route by intent.
[04:39] Luis: That makes sense. Do you support per-route model pinning in the POC?
[04:44] Maya: Yes — routing rules can be configured via our Console or API. For POC we can set simple A/B routing or intent-based routing using a light classifier.
[04:51] Anna: Technical detail — when you say dedicated pool, what are the network requirements for peering? Our infra team needs subnet ranges and security group rules.
[04:59] Jordan: For dedicated we require egress to Redwood control plane on 443 for orchestration, minimal inbound is not required — we initiate connections. For VPC peering we ask for a /28 range and a TLS egress to their NAT. I'll paste a template.
[05:16] Priya: On data residency — we need eu-west only for EU customers. Can you pin region and avoid cross-region fallbacks?
[05:22] Maya: Yes, you can pin a region and we can enforce no-fallback policy; fallback usually helps for reliability but it's optional. We'll note that in the rollout policy.
[05:31] Evan: Can we get the raw bench logs? We want to run our own analysis.
[05:34] Jordan: Absolutely — I'll upload the raw trace plus a summarized csv into the shared drive. Link: https://redwood.test/shared/skylark/bench-20260303 (placeholder)
[05:45] Luis: Perfect. Now, I noticed you mentioned cold starts — do you have a recommended warm-up script?
[05:50] Jordan: Yes, we typically recommend a small continuous warm-up stream that sends periodic short requests to keep KV warm for high-value sessions. We'll provide a script and a config for TTL on cache entries.
[06:03] Anna: Quick infra note — we prefer not to accept inbound peering on our side; would a TLS mutual-auth gateway work?
[06:09] Jordan: Yes, mutual TLS gateway is supported for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we use client cert auth for certain sensitive flows, but usually we route through a customer-hosted gateway.
[06:20] Priya: About the p99 spike — is that more aligned with model compute variability or network jitter?
[06:25] Jordan: From the traces it's a mix: a few spikes were compute (longer sequences hitting recompute branch) and a couple were network. We flagged the two big outliers tied to cache misses which are compute-related.
[06:37] Maya: Let's talk success criteria — Evan, you had mentioned <500ms tail for 300-token replies, and tolerable cost per 1k tokens under $0.40 for this workload. Are those still accurate?
[06:48] Evan: Yes. The $0.40 cap is important for our unit economics on chat receipts.
[06:52] Luis: We also need a pilot decision by end of March so procurement can start contracts.
[06:57] Maya: Understood. For procurement, do you have any RFP or legal timelines?
[07:02] Priya: Procurement wants initial T&Cs by 3/15 and SOC 2 + vendor questionnaire answers earlier if possible.
[07:09] Maya: We'll prioritize the compliance pack and send SOC 2 report and answers to the vendor questionnaire by 3/10.
[07:15] Evan: Great. A couple of more tuning items: can we try a throughput run that simulates Black Friday-ish burst for 60s?
[07:22] Jordan: Yep, we can do a stress run. For the pilot we recommended a 60s ramp with 10x baseline QPS to identify caching and autoscaling thresholds. That will show whether burst capacity meets SLOs.
[07:35] Anna: Do you support autoscaling policies we can tune? We want to avoid over-provisioning.
[07:40] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated supports autoscaling with policy rules based on token/sec and queue depth. We can tune target utilization and keep a small buffer for cheap warm capacity.
[07:51] Luis: Any notes on cost controls? We don't want runaway spend if a bad prompt loops.
[07:56] Maya: You can set per-route budget limits, token caps, and rate limits at the API key level. We'll share a recommended set of guardrails.
[08:06] Evan: On routing policies — are these evaluated client-side or by Redwood? We prefer policies enforced server-side.
[08:12] Jordan: Server-side. Routing is evaluated at the API gateway with rules you can edit. Also supports function/tool-calling style hooks if you want to make the router consult an external intent classifier.
[08:24] Priya: For the eu-west dedicated run you mentioned — are there any pricing differences vs us-west?
[08:29] Maya: There's a small regional delta; we'll put that in the pricing sheet. I'll attach region-specific pricing for eu-west in the follow-up.
[08:36] Luis: OK. I have one last product question — do you do model drift monitoring in the Console as part of Optimize?
[08:42] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Optimize provides regression alerts tied to prompt sets and can trigger rollbacks. We can set thresholds on quality metrics and false-positive rates.
[08:51] Anna: Lovely. Quick clarifying point — the shared drive link requires access; Evan, can you invite Jordan?
[08:57] Evan: Done just now.
[09:00] Maya: Great. Any blockers?
[09:02] Priya: For us, the blockers are KMS confirmation and SSO retry. Once those are resolved we can proceed with peering.
[09:09] Anna: And we need the bench script and raw logs to validate.
[09:13] Jordan: We'll upload both by EOD tomorrow.
[09:16] Luis: Can we schedule the eu-west bench for March 10th at 10am CET?
[09:21] Maya: I'll propose that in calendar after the call.
[09:24] Evan: Sounds good.
[09:26] --- later in the call there's some cross talk and a short digression about billing ---
[30:00] Maya: (brief) On billing, pilot credits will apply to initial usage. We'll include line items in the pricing doc for dedicated reservation vs pay-as-you-go.
[30:20] Priya: Does Redwood require a minimum committed term for dedicated?
[30:24] Maya: Standard is monthly reserved for small pools but annual reserved with discounts for larger capacity. For pilot we can do a month-to-month reserved pool with a small commitment.
[30:34] Evan: Okay that'll help.
[40:00] Jordan: Final technical note — please avoid using very long single-token prompts; split into shorter messages to take advantage of batching and KV reuse. Also avoid embedding large base64 payloads in prompts.
[40:12] Anna: Noted. We'll sanitize the sample set.
[40:16] Maya: All right wrapping up. Recap of agreed items: Jordan uploads bench logs and warm-up script; Maya to send pricing and compliance pack; Priya to retry SSO after Jordan updates SP metadata; Anna to open VPC peering request; schedule eu-west bench 2026-03-10.
[40:38] Luis: Thanks everyone.
[40:40] Evan: Thanks.
[40:42] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email and share artifacts.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-heard words and timestamps approximated; refer to raw logs for exact bench timings.
